Messages.Author: David Pontes
Messages.Body:
Hello again :)

I've been thinking about these two things and could not find anything
to base an answer on:

- According to the system V:tES has been based on, vampires can
enter torpor voluntarily. Nothing on the rulebook (or anywhere I've
looked, for that matter...) gave me a hint as if this could be possible
on the card game. What do you have to say about this?

- It's a main rule that when a vampire commits diablerie, there
may be a call to vote (by any Meth) to burn the Diabolist. It has also
been said that this vote may only be called once per diablerie act. But
if no-one calls a vote immediately after the act has been commited, when
can it be called (note that if we look at the V:TM system, the
Diabolist's aura fades after 40 days or so, so you shouldn't be able to
call it at any time in the future).

Thanks in advance :)

David Pontes

8[

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
David Pontes <l41...@alfa.ist.utl.pt> writes:
> - According to the system V:tES has been based on, vampires can
>enter torpor voluntarily. Nothing on the rulebook (or anywhere I've
>looked, for that matter...) gave me a hint as if this could be possible
>on the card game. What do you have to say about this?

I cannot be done. This would make an unbalanced card (Fame) even more
unbalanced. There is no valid reason to allow this in the card game -
same as not allowing you to choose "no strike" as a strike (very
possible in reality).

> - It's a main rule that when a vampire commits diablerie, there
>may be a call to vote (by any Meth) to burn the Diabolist. It has also
>been said that this vote may only be called once per diablerie act. But
>if no-one calls a vote immediately after the act has been commited, when
>can it be called (note that if we look at the V:TM system, the
>Diabolist's aura fades after 40 days or so, so you shouldn't be able to
>call it at any time in the future).

It must happen immediately (before the next action or the end of the minion
phase). Note that each action represents what the minions are doing over
the course of approximately a game month, so this isn't too far from the
VtM 40-day specification (which I have only your post to go on).

Note that you can't diablerize whith one vampire and then "talk fast"
to begin your next minion action - anyone may request that you wait.
It is usually good form to ask if anyone wants to call a bloodhunt
before going on - since someone almost always will.

Messages.Body:
In article <Pine.OSF.3.91.960227122229...@alfa.ist.utl.pt>, David Pontes <l41...@alfa.ist.utl.pt> writes:
>
> Hello again :)
>
> I've been thinking about these two things and could not find anything
> to base an answer on:
>

> - According to the system V:tES has been based on, vampires can
> enter torpor voluntarily. Nothing on the rulebook (or anywhere I've
> looked, for that matter...) gave me a hint as if this could be possible
> on the card game. What do you have to say about this?
>

You can with Fortitude. Dawn Operation, and especially Force of Will
will send you to Torpor. The reason behind the no strictly voluntary torpor,
is strictly game balance. It is already possible to mess up peoples'
Malkavians beyond belief with Malkavian Dementation. Were you able to simply
send them to torpor with no save and no extra cards, the Malkavians would be
too hosed.

> - It's a main rule that when a vampire commits diablerie, there
> may be a call to vote (by any Meth) to burn the Diabolist. It has also
> been said that this vote may only be called once per diablerie act. But
> if no-one calls a vote immediately after the act has been commited, when
> can it be called (note that if we look at the V:TM system, the
> Diabolist's aura fades after 40 days or so, so you shouldn't be able to
> call it at any time in the future).
>

Actually, your Aura fades in 3 months, not 1.5, so it would be logical
that you could call a bloodhunt on a Diabolist for the rest of the game.
However, it is assumed that if noone calls a bloodhunt, then it is simple
general acquiesence to the diablery, and it can never be called again.
